## Role Identity
Senior Product Designer & Front-End Prototyper specialized in turning product ideas, feature specs, user stories, or rough screenshots into **fully functional, browser-runnable HTML mockups**. Expertise spans UI/UX composition, component systems, vanilla-JS state management, and mocking backend endpoints + data so the mockup *behaves* like the real product instead of looking like a static picture.

**Goal:** Produce mockups that open in any browser and actually work — clickable navigation, working forms with validation, lists that filter/sort/paginate, data that loads from a mocked API, state that persists — using inline scripts plus public CDN libraries where they genuinely help.

**Domain Focus:** codx-junior – Modern AI Assistant Chat Platform with Dark-First Aesthetic

---

## 1. CORE PRINCIPLES

- **Functional over static.** A mockup is *not* a screenshot. Every interactive control must respond: clicks, typing, hovers, navigation, state changes.
- **Single entry file by default.** Everything that can be inline is inline. Multi-file (`.html` + `.js` + `.css`) is allowed only when a build-free split improves clarity — **never** require a bundler, `npm install`, or a dev server.

- **Public CDNs are allowed and encouraged.** Tailwind Play CDN, Alpine.js, htmx, Chart.js, Lucide icons, etc. — **pin the version** and make sure the layout still holds if a CDN fails to load.
- **Realistic data, plausible flows.** Seed data must read like production. Every primary action should produce a visible result — never leave a button that does nothing.
- **Mock the states, not just the happy path.** Loading, empty, error, and edge cases are part of the mockup, not an afterthought.
- **Self-documenting.** Mark every fake boundary with comments (`// MOCK:` / `<!-- MOCK -->`) so a developer knows exactly what is simulated.

---

## 2. MOCKUP ARCHITECTURE (MANDATORY)

Every mockup MUST follow this skeleton so state, mock API, and rendering stay decoupled:

"""
ChatEventBridge — attaches AgentRunContext events to the chat response message
and persists it on EVERY change (crash-safe).

During an AI turn the SmolAgent emits :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentEvent`

chat messages:

      (one entry per tool call, updated in place: running → done/error). Each
      event also carries the tool's user-facing ``output`` so tool output can be
      rendered collapsed/hidden instead of polluting ``Message.content``.
    * ``response_message.lifecycle_events`` → list of :class:`LifeCycleEvent`
      (one entry per agent run, updated in place)

Tool output
-----------
TOOL_END events carry the dual-response tool's user-facing ``output``
(``ToolResponse.user_response``). The bridge stores it on the matching
:class:`ToolEvent` (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of it being merged into the
chat content, so the client decides how to display it. Cached tool calls do not
re-emit output (the first execution already delivered it).

----------------------
On every event change the response message is:

    1. **Persisted immediately** via the ChatManager granular merge-safe
       methods (``add_message`` on first change, ``update_message`` after).
       If the process dies mid-run, every event received so far — including
       tool errors, run errors and aggregated analytics — is already on disk.
    2. **Streamed** to clients in real time via the EventManager so the UI
       can render tool progress live.

ADDED — streamed-chunk crash-safety (:meth:`maybe_persist_stream`):
    Streaming callbacks may call :meth:`maybe_persist_stream` on every flush;
    the bridge persists the response message AT MOST once per
    ``STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` (monotonic clock). A hard kill
    therefore loses at most that many seconds of streamed partial text while
    keeping disk I/O bounded.

ADDED — auxiliary message crash-safety (:meth:`persist_message`):
    Any auxiliary message produced mid-run (e.g. hidden reasoning messages)

```md design/README.md
# codx-junior — Design Documentation

Corporate image and UI/UX foundation for **codx-junior**, derived from an audit of the
shipping product (`client/` — project `codx-junior-ui`).

> **Status:** v0.1 — *baseline definition*. Everything here describes either
> (a) what the product does **today**, verified in code, or (b) a **decision
> proposal** to close a gap. Each statement is labelled so the two never get
> confused.

> **Start here — [`playbook/index.html`](playbook/index.html).** The whole design system on
> one self-contained page: live component specimens, dark/light toggle, print-ready layout.
> Hand it to any developer before they write UI code.

---

## Why this folder exists

codx-junior grew feature-first: 400+ Vue components, several parallel shells
(desktop dockview, mobile app shell, company shell, solopreneur shell) and three
different colour palettes that leaked into the codebase over time. The product
works, but it does not yet look like *one company*.

This folder is the single place where the corporate image is defined, so that:

- a new screen can be designed without inventing new colours, spacing or copy;
- a designer and a developer can agree on a spec without a meeting;
- rebrand work (logo, palette, marketing site) has a contract to break *on purpose*.

---

## How to read it

| Folder | Contents | Audience |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `playbook/` | **The playbook** (`index.html`) — this whole folder on one page, with rendered specimens | Developers, new joiners |
| `resources/` | **Official artwork** — `logo.png` (the mark, 267 × 266 PNG + alpha) and `me-and-codx-junior.png` (brand photograph). Embedded by the playbook, taken from here, never re-exported | Everyone |
| `00-audit/` | What the current UI actually is, with file-level evidence | Designers, tech leads |
| `01-brand/` | Brand platform, logo, colour, typography, voice — the *corporate image* | Everyone, marketing included |
| `02-design-system/` | Foundations (space, radius, motion, layering) and component specs | Designers, frontend |
| `03-ux/` | Information architecture, navigation model, accessibility | Designers, PMs, frontend |
| `04-assets/` | Asset production rules: formats, sizes, naming, export | Design, marketing |
| `05-governance/` | Ownership, versioning, review checklist, adoption roadmap | Leads |
| `06-calendar/` | **Feature design** — agenda/calendar manager: deep analysis, clickable prototype, API fixtures. Design only, no code changed | Product, frontend, backend |
| `tokens/` | `design-tokens.json` — machine-readable source for the values above | Frontend |

Reading order for a newcomer: **audit → brand platform → colour → typography →
foundations → components → IA**.

---

## Ground rules

1. **The code is the current truth; this folder is the target truth.** When they
   disagree, the documents say which one wins.
2. **No new colour, radius or spacing value without a token.** If a value is
   missing, add a token here first, then use it.
3. **Every doc is versioned with the product**, not separately. See
   `05-governance/design-ops.md`.
4. **Numbers beat adjectives.** "16px, 8px grid, 4.5:1" is a spec; "modern and
   clean" is not.

# Colour System

**Status:** tokens defined here; **not yet wired into the codebase**
(see `00-audit/ui-audit.md` §2). Until they are, the app runs on stock daisyUI themes.

Contrast ratios below are computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula
against the stated backgrounds. They are reproducible: keep the function in
`design/tokens/contrast.md` honest if values change.

---

## 1. The error we are correcting

Three palettes currently coexist:

| Source | Primary | Problem |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client/src/assets/main.css` (live) | `#CC0099` | Applied only to `.codx-primary` / `.text-codx-secondary` |
| `client/src/assets/daisy-override.css` (dead) | `#CC049C` | Re-tints 35 themes with a *near-miss* of the brand magenta |
| `client/.codx/profiles/Designer/Designer.md` | `#6366F1` (indigo) | A completely different, cool-toned palette |

`#CC0099` vs `#CC049C` is a **3/255 difference in one channel** — invisible to the eye,
but it means "brand colour" is not a single value in the repo. The Designer profile's
indigo was never implemented and must be retired.

**Decision:** `#CC0099` is the brand magenta. `#CC049C` is retired. Indigo is deleted
from the design vocabulary.

---

## 2. Brand ramps (source of truth)

### Magenta (primary signature)

| Token | Hex | OKLCH | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand.magenta.50` | `#FFF0FA` | `oklch(97% 0.02 330)` | Tinted background (light) |
| `brand.magenta.100` | `#FFD6F0` | `oklch(93% 0.05 330)` | Selected row (light) |
| `brand.magenta.200` | `#FFAEE0` | `oklch(86% 0.10 330)` | Borders on tint |
| `brand.magenta.300` | `#FF80CE` | `oklch(77% 0.17 330)` | Dark-mode hover |
| `brand.magenta.400` | `#FF69B4` | `oklch(72% 0.19 340)` | **Primary text/icon on dark** |
| `brand.magenta.500` | `#F530A8` | `oklch(65% 0.25 330)` | Dark-mode primary fill |
| `brand.magenta.600` | **`#CC0099`** | `oklch(56% 0.28 330)` | **Brand. Primary fill on light** |
| `brand.magenta.700` | `#A3007A` | `oklch(48% 0.24 330)` | Pressed |
| `brand.magenta.800` | `#7A005B` | `oklch(38% 0.19 330)` | Deep accent, charts |
| `brand.magenta.900` | `#4D0039` | `oklch(26% 0.12 330)` | Tinted dark background |

The **dark-theme primary is `oklch(65% 0.32 320)`** (`brand.magenta.500`-ish): the same
hue, lightness raised so it can carry text on the dark canvas. This is the single most
important colour decision in the system — see §5.

### Purple (secondary, depth)

| Token | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brand.purple.500` | `#B000B0` | Secondary fill (light) |
| `brand.purple.600` | **`#8F008F`** | Brand secondary. Depth, gradients, chart series 2 |
| `brand.purple.700` | `#6B006B` | Gradient end, pressed |
| `brand.purple.400` | `#C24AC2` | Secondary text on dark |

> `#8F008F` on the dark canvas is **1.8:1** — it is a *fill and gradient* colour only.
> Never use it for text on dark.
